Photographer: Erik Flyg/Bloomberg via Getty Images](https://image.cnbcfm.com/api/v1/image/108416314-1792099131626-gettyimages-2299775963-SWEDEN_NVIDIA.jpeg?v=1792099225&w=1858&h=1045&vtcrop=y)
Kazakhstan may not be the first place that comes to mind when thinking about the global artificial intelligence boom, but several Big Tech companies have taken interest — including Nvidia.
Sitting in a fireside chat in Astana with Zhaslan Madiyev, Kazakhstan’s deputy prime minister and minister of artificial intelligence and digital development, Huang highlighted the country’s role.
The visit comes as Kazakhstan seeks to attract billions of dollars in technology investment and position itself as a regional hub for artificial intelligence.
## Kazakhstan’s multibillion-dollar AI ambitions At the center of the initiative is [Data Center Valley](https://primeminister.kz/en/news/data-center-valley-kazakhstan-government-firebird-and-nvidia-sign-10-billion-package-of-agreements-in-artificial-intelligence-31516), a planned AI infrastructure hub in Ekibastuz with 300 megawatts of power capacity is already available with plans to expand to 1 gigawatt.
## China’s growing connection to Central Asia This year’s SCO event on artificial intelligence [took](https://eng.sectsco.org/20261003/2547187.html) place earlier this month in Kazakhstan’s capital, Astana, bringing together representatives from member states to discuss national AI strategies, regulation and opportunities for technological cooperation.

item.title: U.S.-Latin America Day of Artificial Intelligence symposium celebrates high school student creativity, innovation
item.description:
# University of Illinois System News ## Images High school students from the United States and Latin America showcased their creativity and perspectives on artificial intelligence during the [U.S.-Latin America Day of Artificial Intelligence](https://www.busfin.uillinois.edu/day_of_artificial_intelligence), a virtual symposium co-hosted by the University of Illinois Springfield and the University of Illinois System’s Illinois Mexican and Mexican-American Students (I-MMÁS) initiative.
Held on Oct. 15, the symposium brought together students, educators, researchers and industry leaders to explore artificial intelligence applications across science, engineering, business, education and digital communication.
The student submissions reflected diverse perspectives on artificial intelligence and demonstrated how emerging technologies can serve as tools for creative expression, problem-solving and exploration of real-world issues.
The speakers brought perspectives from academia and industry, illustrating the interdisciplinary nature of artificial intelligence and its growing influence on research, innovation and professional practice.
